CausalChain: Radiotherapy → Tumor cell death and release of immunogenic factors → Acute increase of circulating TGF‐β1 in STIE → TGF‐β1 acts on circulating and infiltrating CD8+ T cells inducing a pre‐exhausted, reprogrammable state → Single‐cell transcriptomics detects this transient T cell signature → Timed PD-1 blockade reinvigorates these T cells → Enhanced anti-tumor immune response
Hypothesis: Administering PD‐1 inhibitors at a strategic post‐radiotherapy window—when radiotherapy‐induced circulating TGF‐β1 has primed a pool of pre‐exhausted CD8+ T cells in the systemic tumor immune environment—will enhance anti-tumor immunity and improve clinical outcomes in solid tumors.
Abstract: Recent advances in single‐cell and spatial transcriptomics have unveiled the complex interplay between the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and the systemic tumor immune environment (STIE) that governs responses to immunotherapy. Here, we propose that radiotherapy induces a transient increase in circulating transforming growth factor‐β1 (TGF‐β1) and other immunomodulatory signals, which in turn drive a reprogramming of circulating CD8+ T cells into a pre‐exhausted state. These primed T cells, as revealed by single‐cell transcriptomic profiles, can be effectively reinvigorated by appropriate timing of PD‐1 blockade, leading to enhanced anti‐tumor immunity. This hypothesis suggests that synchronizing PD‐1 inhibitor administration with the radiotherapy‐induced STIE remodeling could optimize immunotherapeutic outcomes in solid tumors.
